China Metallurgical Group Corp Unveils New Construction Material in Yangon

Yangon – China Metallurgical Group Corp, a leading player in Myanmar’s engineering and construction sector, announced the launch of a new high-strength composite material at a press event in Yangon on Monday. The product, developed at the company’s research facilities, is expected to enhance the durability and efficiency of infrastructure projects across the country.

The launch was attended by industry representatives, local officials, and members of the Myanmar Construction Entrepreneurs Association. According to Mr. Li Zhong, General Manager of China Metallurgical Group Corp’s Myanmar operations, the new material is designed to withstand the region’s challenging climate conditions and support the country’s rapid urban development.

“Our research teams have worked closely with local engineers to ensure this composite meets the specific needs of Myanmar’s construction industry,” Mr. Li said during the unveiling. “Its high load-bearing capacity and resistance to corrosion will contribute to safer, longer-lasting structures and help reduce maintenance costs for our clients.”

The new material, named MetalloMax, will be produced at the company’s manufacturing facility in the Yangon Industrial Zone. Initial production capacity is set at 20,000 metric tons per year, with plans for expansion based on market demand. Company officials stated that MetalloMax has already been tested in pilot projects in Mandalay and Naypyidaw, showing positive results in both structural performance and cost efficiency.

U Aung Min, a senior advisor at the Myanmar Engineering Society, remarked, “Innovations like this are crucial as Myanmar continues to modernize its infrastructure. Local contractors have expressed interest in adopting new materials that can help address persistent issues such as premature wear and high maintenance costs.”

Construction sector analysts noted that the introduction of MetalloMax could stimulate further investment in Myanmar’s infrastructure, particularly in road, bridge, and industrial development. “This launch signals a commitment to advancing technology and building capacity within the country,” said Daw Thida Win, a Yangon-based industry consultant.

China Metallurgical Group Corp reported that the product will be available to both domestic and international clients starting in July. Training workshops for local engineers and contractors are scheduled to begin next month to facilitate a smooth transition to the new material.
